A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Subset-Norm and Subspace-Momentum research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite the changed title and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLaMA pretraining experiments, GLUE fine-tuning results, optimizer ablations, memory measurements, and gradient-noise analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds UltraFeedback fine-tuning, vision evaluations, runtime measurements, and repeated-seed analyses.

M1.justification: The core SN/SM updates and main SVD implementation remain unchanged; AdaGradSNSM already appeared in v1. However, v2 Appendix B.8 introduces online-PCA and Oja subspace-update variants that retain optimizer statistics during updates. These are limited procedural extensions to the existing momentum framework.

E1.justification: C4 pretraining and GLUE fine-tuning are retained. V2 adds LLaMA 7B supervised fine-tuning on UltraFeedback, CIFAR10/CIFAR100 image classification, and DiT-L/2 image-generation experiments. This substantially expands data and task coverage beyond v1's language experiments. The diffusion experiment's dataset is not identified.

E2.justification: V2 Table 8 adds reported pretraining comparisons with FLORA, LoRA, and ReLoRA. AdaGrad and AdaGradm join the main multi-scale comparison, although both existed in v1's ablations. Table 13 also adds Gaussian, OPCA, and Oja projection comparators. Adam-mini receives discussion but no corresponding reported experimental comparison.

E3.justification: V2 adds a fixed-1.3B-token batch-size sweep from 4 to 1024 alongside v1's retained fixed-step experiment, plus cross-scale fixed-subspace and longer-gap protocols. New SFT and vision experiments introduce distinct budgets and metrics. Table 3 changes the reported 350M AdaGradSNm/AdaGradmSN learning rate from 1 to 2. The main pretraining budgets otherwise persist.

E4.justification: V2 extends subset-size ablations to 130M, tests projection refresh schedules across model sizes, and investigates online/streaming subspace selection. Appendix C.3 and Figure 18 test whether the architectural grouping heuristic concentrates gradient noise. Fixed-token batch-size analyses address a control missing from v1. Existing clipping, rank-gap, and momentum/step-size ablations are retained, often relocated.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix B.11 introduces three-seed performance experiments with means and standard deviations in Tables 17–18, and discloses seed matching across comparisons. V1 estimates gradient-noise variance but does not report comparable training-run uncertainty. The new reporting does not establish that all retained results were rerun or averaged.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive results, including 1B AdaGradSNSM perplexity 13.96, UltraFeedback final perplexity 2.580 for rank-32 SNSM, vision scores, timings, and seed summaries. The 350M AdaGradSNm/AdaGradmSN entry changes from 16.99 at learning rate 1 to 17.14 at learning rate 2, so this is not a same-setting performance change. V2 Table 8 conflicts with Table 3 for 1B AdamSNSM (13.96 versus 14.05) and 350M GaLore (20.51 versus 18.95).

T1.justification: V1 Theorem 2's SM guarantee uses eta = 1/(alpha sqrt(T)); v2 Theorem 4.1 uses a capped, noise-dependent step size and obtains an O(1/T) deterministic term with an O(sigma/sqrt(T)) stochastic term. Appendix D revises the derivation and removes its separate bounded-variance expectation bound. The Subset-Norm theorem and Appendix E proof remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: V2's abstract and conclusion explicitly extend the empirical claims to LLM fine-tuning, and its contribution statement emphasizes benefits across AdaGrad-based optimizers as well as Adam. The two central techniques, memory-scaling claims, convergence guarantees, and headline token-efficiency and memory benefits remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds hypotheses connecting momentum benefits to subspace noise, explains the grouping heuristic through architectural noise correlations, and attributes GaLore switching spikes to incompatible optimizer statistics. It discusses SFT's SVD runtime cost and activation/gradient memory bottlenecks, and qualifies the revised SM rate as requiring problem-parameter knowledge. Higher-order tensor projections become an explicit applicability limitation; the unresolved combined SNSM guarantee was already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: V2 adds a PyTorch implementation link and hardware, model identifiers, learning-rate grids, and timing configurations for new experiments. The existing optimizer pseudocode, memory-measurement listing, and core pretraining details largely persist or relocate to Appendix A. Some new documentation remains inconsistent: the CIFAR prose says no update gap, while Table 11 specifies g = 1000.

R1.justification: V2 substantively positions the methods against Adam-mini and AdaMeM, discusses second-order approaches including Shampoo, Sophia, and SOAP, and incorporates momentum and online-PCA literature. It also removes v1's citation and disclosure identifying the preliminary Subset-Norm workshop version. These changes extend and revise the relationship to closely related research.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: optimizer background moves into Preliminaries, related work moves near the end, experimental setup moves to Appendix A, and several main-text ablations move into Appendix B. Contributions, interpretations, and future-work passages are rewritten, and the title changes.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, with substantial table restructuring and relocation. Figure 1 becomes a single panel on the first page; v2 adds an SN schematic, new analysis plots, and numerous experimental tables. The old noise histogram is retained as Figure 11, while Figure 3 gains a secondary axis showing noisy-coordinate fractions.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central efficiency and robustness claims. Table 9 adds measured runtimes and realistic peak memory; Table 17 controls total data when varying batch size, and Tables 17–18 report three-run variability. These address important gaps in v1's token-based speed evidence and fixed-step batch analyses. Added SFT and vision experiments broaden validation. Conflicting values in Tables 3 and 8 and inconsistent CIFAR settings weaken specific new results, but do not outweigh these substantial evidential gains.
